title: Gérard Depardieu
wiki_lead:
Gérard Xavier Marcel Depardieu (UK: , US: , French: [ʒeʁaʁ ɡzavje maʁsɛl dəpaʁdjø] ; born 27 December 1948) is a French actor. Considered an icon of French cinema in the same way as Jean Gabin and Alain Delon, he has appeared in over 200 films since 1967, mostly in leading roles. Depardieu has worked with more than 150 film directors, including major filmmakers such as François Truffaut, Alain Resnais, Ridley Scott, Peter Weir and Bernardo Bertolucci. He is the second highest-grossing actor in the history of French cinema behind Louis de Funès, with roughly 60 of his films selling more than one million admissions in France. He has portrayed various well-known historical and fictitious figures, including Cyrano de Bergerac, Georges Danton, Christopher Columbus, Jean Valjean, Edmond Dantès and Porthos, as well as Obelix in four of the live action Asterix films. Beyond acting, Depardieu is a film producer, businessman and vineyard owner. He has occasionally directed films and performed as a singer. His body of work includes extensive television productions, several records and, as of 2025, 19 stage plays and 9 books.
Growing up in poverty in Châteauroux, central  France, Depardieu experienced a difficult youth and was a juvenile delinquent before settling in Paris, where he became an actor. His breakthrough came in 1974 with the film Going Places, which propelled him to overnight stardom. He quickly established himself as a major figure in European cinema and demonstrated his versatility by appearing in a wide variety of films, spanning both mainstream and auteur productions. He has received acclaim for his performances in The Last Metro (1980), where he won the César Award for Best Actor, Police (1985), for which he won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor, Jean de Florette (1986), and Cyrano de Bergerac (1990), where he won the Best Actor award at the Cannes Film Festival and his second César Award for Best Actor as well as garnering a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actor. He started a Hollywood career with Green Card (1990), winning a Golden Globe Award for Best Actor, and later appeared in several high-budget English-language films, including 1492: Conquest of Paradise (1992), The Man in the Iron Mask (1998), and Life of Pi (2012).
Besides his acting accolades, Depardieu has garnered various honors, including appointments as a Chevalier of the Légion d'honneur and the Ordre national du Mérite. He was granted citizenship of Russia in January 2013. During the early 2010s, his tax exile in Russia and his support of Vladimir Putin caused controversy in France.
Depardieu was accused of sexual misconduct as early as the 1990s, though this did not develop into formal complaints until the late 2010s. In December 2020, French authorities charged him with rape. Depardieu denied any wrongdoing but a number of controversies, not limited to the accusations of rape, have since damaged his popularity in France and abroad. This resulted in several of his honors being rescinded in 2023, notably the National Order of Quebec. In May 2025, he was convicted of sexual assault against two women in a separate case. He appealed his sentencing, but withdrew his appeal in November 2026.

His breakthrough came in the 1970s with roles in films like Les Valseuses (1974), establishing him as a leading figure in French cinema, followed by critically acclaimed performances in Cyrano de Bergerac (1990), for which he won the Best Actor award at the Cannes Film Festival and received an Academy Award nomination. Depardieu's international appeal expanded with English-language films such as Green Card (1990), securing a Golden Globe, and collaborations like 1492: Conquest of Paradise (1992), while his stage work and directorial efforts further diversified his contributions to the arts. Beyond cinema, Depardieu has been a vocal public figure, notably relocating from France in 2012 amid disputes over a proposed 75% supertax on high earners, initially to Belgium and subsequently obtaining Russian citizenship in 2013 granted by President Vladimir Putin, reflecting his friendship with the Russian leader cultivated through visits and shared interests. In 2022, despite this rapport, he publicly condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine as a "fratricidal war," urging negotiation over escalation. Depardieu's personal life has intersected with legal controversies, including a May 2025 conviction for sexual assault related to a 2021 incident on a film set, resulting in an 18-month suspended sentence that became final after he withdrew his appeal in November 2026, amid multiple allegations from over 20 women spanning decades, with a separate rape case still pending.
